newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2980 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2983 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based China foreign exchange interbank market after three days of losses.
Dealers said that constant dollar-selling gave firm support to the local currency, but sluggish trading confined it to a narrow range.
The yuan opened unchanged at an intraday low of 8.2983 and moved around 8.2980 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2975 around mid-session.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2980, traders said.
One dealer said that yuan sentiment was still bullish, although it had fallen slightly in the past three days. "The increased demand at the year-end has strengthened the yuan."
A second dealer said the closure of most world foreign exchange markets during the Christmas holiday made the dollar less attractive. "This has indirectly supported the yuan."
Dealers said they believed the yuan would consolidate around the 8.2980 level on Thursday.
The yuan closed up at 7.2350 from 7.2490 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0720 from 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
